name: Eyebrow Naturalness
description: Assesses individual eyebrow hair strand rendering quality and bilateral symmetry deviations, targeting known weaknesses of face generation models in reproducing fine facial hair detail.
mechanism:
This method analyzes eyebrow movement patterns for deepfake detection:

1. **Eyebrow Landmark Tracking**: Precise eyebrow landmarks are tracked per frame, measuring: arch height, arch position, medial endpoint, lateral endpoint, and brow thickness. These geometric parameters capture eyebrow shape and position with sub-pixel accuracy.

2. **Brow Movement Dynamics**: Eyebrow movements are analyzed for naturalness — raise speed, lowering speed, asymmetric movement patterns. Natural brow movements follow physiological constraints of the frontalis and corrugator muscles. Deepfake generators may produce brow movements that are too symmetric, too fast/slow, or follow unnatural trajectories.

3. **Brow-Expression Coordination**: Eyebrow position is tightly coupled with facial expressions — surprise raises brows, anger lowers them, skepticism raises one brow. The method verifies temporal coordination between brow position and other facial features (eyes, mouth). Deepfakes may show decoupled brow-expression dynamics.

4. **Brow Texture & Hair Detail**: Individual eyebrow hairs should be visible in high-resolution video and maintain consistent texture across frames. The method analyzes brow texture quality — AI generators often produce smoothed brow regions lacking individual hair detail or showing temporally inconsistent hair rendering.

5. **Bilateral Brow Symmetry**: Natural eyebrows show characteristic bilateral asymmetry that remains consistent. The method tracks left-right brow asymmetry — deepfakes may produce brow movements with incorrect asymmetry patterns (too symmetric or varying asymmetry frame-to-frame). The score combines dynamic naturalness, coordination, texture quality, and symmetry analysis.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through eyebrow naturalness analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Rossler, A. et al. (2019). FaceForensics++: Learning to Detect Manipulated Facial Images. ICCV.
Matern, F. et al. (2019). Exploiting Visual Artifacts to Expose Deepfakes. WACVW.
